text: HTTP request retry: retry transient network errors with exponential backoff and random jitter. Bound the number of attempts.
HTTP request timeouts: set connection and read timeouts. A deadline prevents slow upstream services from blocking a worker forever.
Queue retry policy: retry failed jobs with backoff. Route poison messages to a dead letter queue after the attempt limit.
Idempotency keys make repeated payment requests safe. A server stores the first result so a retry does not create a second charge.
Database indexes speed filtered reads. A composite index supports queries on its leading columns, at the cost of extra writes and storage.
Use an EXPLAIN query plan to inspect database scans. An index can avoid a full table scan for selective lookup queries.
Pagination with a cursor uses a stable ordering and a continuation token. Cursor pagination avoids skipping records when new rows arrive.
Offset pagination uses LIMIT and OFFSET. Large offsets require scanning discarded rows and can become expensive.
BM25 is a lexical retrieval ranking function using term frequency, document length and inverse document frequency. It matches words rather than embeddings.
Dense embeddings map documents and queries into vectors. Nearest neighbor search can retrieve paraphrases with different vocabulary.
A retrieval evaluation needs relevance judgments. Recall measures coverage of relevant documents; reciprocal rank rewards the first relevant result.
Normalized discounted cumulative gain evaluates ranked retrieval results. nDCG discounts lower positions and divides by an ideal relevance ordering.
A cache stores computed results with a time to live. Cache invalidation removes stale values after the source data changes.
A cache stampede happens when many requests refill one expired key. A per-key lock or single flight mechanism prevents duplicate work.
Structured logging records events with named fields such as request ID and error code. Never log credentials or secret tokens.
Distributed tracing follows one request across services using trace IDs and spans. Traces help explain latency between service boundaries.
